commands.author: Pick-cat

target.title: fix(qa-lab): reject hex/exponent Telegram SUT uid env values
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Telegram QA SUT env integers (`OPENCLAW_QA_TELEGRAM_SUT_UID`, `GID`, and cleanup timeout) accepted JavaScript-only forms such as `0x3e9` and `1e3` via `Number(...)`. Those values were treated as valid UIDs/timeouts even though the env contract promises a positive decimal integer.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Reuse `parseStrictPositiveInteger` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/number-runtime` — the same helper qa-lab CLI flags already use — inside `parseSutId`.
- Keep the existing `must be a positive integer` error text.
- `Number("0x3e9")` → 1001, `Number("1e3")` → 1000 pass `Number.isSafeInteger` — the old guard did not protect against hex/exponent.
- `parseStrictPositiveInteger` enforces `/^\+?\d+$/` — rejects hex, exponent, fraction, empty.

Collision check: searched open PRs for `parseSutId`, `cli.runtime.ts`, `OPENCLAW_QA_TELEGRAM_SUT_UID`; no same-file or same-problem open PR was found.

## User Impact

Malformed hex/exponent Telegram SUT identity/timeout env values now fail fast with `OPENCLAW_QA_TELEGRAM_SUT_UID must be a positive integer.` instead of silently mapping to a different decimal integer. Ordinary decimal env values are unchanged.

## Verification

- Exact head: `19998f74762b7798d8ddb65fb2e698c3cceee428`
- `oxfmt --check extensions/qa-lab/src/live-transports/telegram/cli.runtime.ts extensions/qa-lab/src/cli.runtime.test.ts` — passed.
- `oxlint extensions/qa-lab/src/live-transports/telegram/cli.runtime.ts extensions/qa-lab/src/cli.runtime.test.ts` — passed; exit 0.
- `git diff --check` — passed; exit 0.
- Focused tests:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qa-lab/src/cli.runtime.test.ts -- --run --reporter=verbose
```

```
 ✓ extensions/qa-lab/src/cli.runtime.test.ts > telegram SUT strict id parsing > parseSutId rejects 0x3e9 (hex)
 ✓ extensions/qa-lab/src/cli.runtime.test.ts > telegram SUT strict id parsing > parseSutId rejects 1e3 (exponent)
 ✓ extensions/qa-lab/src/cli.runtime.test.ts > telegram SUT strict id parsing > parseSutId rejects 1001.5 (fraction)
 ✓ extensions/qa-lab/src/cli.runtime.test.ts > telegram SUT strict id parsing > parseSutId accepts "1001" (decimal)
 ✓ extensions/qa-lab/src/cli.runtime.test.ts > telegram SUT strict id parsing > parseSutId accepts "1" (decimal)
 ✓ extensions/qa-lab/src/cli.runtime.test.ts > telegram SUT strict id parsing > parseSutId rejects "" (empty)
 ✓ extensions/qa-lab/src/cli.runtime.test.ts > telegram SUT strict id parsing > parseSutId rejects " " (whitespace)
 ✓ extensions/qa-lab/src/cli.runtime.test.ts > telegram SUT strict id parsing > parseSutId rejects "0" (zero)
 ✓ extensions/qa-lab/src/cli.runtime.test.ts > telegram SUT strict id parsing > parseSutId rejects "-1" (negative)
```

- Full suite: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qa-lab/src/cli.runtime.test.ts -- --run` — 102 passed, 0 failed.
- Mutation check: temporarily reverted `cli.runtime.ts` to `Number()`-based `parseSutId` → case 4 failed (old code accepted "0x3e9" as UID=1001) → restore → all 18/18 pass.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: `parseSutId` rejects hex (`0x3e9`), exponent (`1e3`), and fraction (`1001.5`) env values instead of silently coercing them via `Number()`.

Real environment tested: Linux, Node v22.22.0, local loopback (no live Telegram credentials needed).

Exact commands run:

```bash
node --import tsx proof-qa-telegram-sut-strict-int.mts
```

Observed output after fix:

```text
node=v22.22.0
head=19998f74762b7798d8ddb65fb2e698c3cceee428

[case 1] negative control - Number() accepts hex/exponent/fraction
  ok: Number("0x3e9") = 1001 for UID - old code would accept
  info: env=OPENCLAW_QA_TELEGRAM_SUT_UID input=0x3e9 Number()=1001 (would be accepted as UID)
  ok: Number("1e3") = 1000 for GID - old code would accept
  info: env=OPENCLAW_QA_TELEGRAM_SUT_GID input=1e3 Number()=1000 (would be accepted as GID)
  ok: Number("0x3e8") = 1000 for cleanup timeout - old code would accept
  info: env=OPENCLAW_QA_TELEGRAM_SUT_CLEANUP_TIMEOUT_MS input=0x3e8 Number()=1000 (would be accepted as cleanup timeout)
  ok: Number("1001.5") = 1001.5 for UID with fraction - old code would accept
  info: env=OPENCLAW_QA_TELEGRAM_SUT_UID input=1001.5 Number()=1001.5 (would be accepted as UID with fraction)
  ok: Number.isSafeInteger(Number("0x3e9")) === true - old guard passed
  ok: Number.isSafeInteger(Number("1e3")) === true - old guard passed

[case 2] positive control - parseStrictPositiveInteger rejects non-decimal
  ok: parseStrictPositiveInteger("0x3e9") returns undefined (rejected)
  ok: parseStrictPositiveInteger("1e3") returns undefined (rejected)
  ok: parseStrictPositiveInteger("1001.5") returns undefined (rejected)
  ok: parseStrictPositiveInteger("0x3e8") returns undefined (rejected)
  ok: parseStrictPositiveInteger("") returns undefined (rejected)
  ok: parseStrictPositiveInteger(" ") returns undefined (rejected)

[case 3] valid response - decimal strings parse correctly
  ok: OPENCLAW_QA_TELEGRAM_SUT_UID parses to 1001
  ok: OPENCLAW_QA_TELEGRAM_SUT_GID parses to 1002
  ok: OPENCLAW_QA_TELEGRAM_SUT_CLEANUP_TIMEOUT_MS parses to 60000
  ok: OPENCLAW_QA_TELEGRAM_SUT_CLEANUP_TIMEOUT_MS parses to 30000
  ok: OPENCLAW_QA_TELEGRAM_SUT_UID parses to 1

[case 4] full CLI chain - malformed UID rejects before gateway startup
  ok: malformed UID "0x3e9" throws "must be a positive integer" before gateway startup
  info: error=OPENCLAW_QA_TELEGRAM_SUT_UID must be a positive integer.

=== Summary ===
ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS: 18 passed, 0 failed
```

Evidence:
- Old guard `Number.isSafeInteger(Number("0x3e9"))` returns `true` — hex values were accepted as valid UIDs.
- Old guard `Number.isSafeInteger(Number("1e3"))` returns `true` — exponent values were accepted.
- New `parseStrictPositiveInteger` rejects all 6 malformed forms: `0x3e9`, `1e3`, `1001.5`, `0x3e8`, `""`, `" "`.
- Full CLI chain proof: malformed UID `"0x3e9"` is rejected BEFORE gateway startup, not after.
- Decimal strings (`"1001"`, `"1002"`, `"60000"`, `"1"`) still parse correctly — no regression.
- Mutation check: reverting to old `Number()` code causes case 4 to fail (17/18 vs 18/18).

What was not tested: live Telegram QA Crabbox/Mantis runs; remote provider auth; this is SUT env parsing only.

## Risk / Compatibility

Low. The env error message already promised "must be a positive integer"; sibling qa-lab CLI parsers already use `parseStrictPositiveInteger`; decimal env values are unchanged. No config key changes, no CLI flag changes, no new dependencies.
